title: Parallel Lines, Transversals and Triangle Angles
seo_title: Grade 8 Parallel Lines and Transversals Worksheets (TEKS 8.8D, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.8D use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.8D: parallel lines and transversals, angle pairs, triangle angle sums, exterior angles and angle equations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; same-side interior angles add to 180°.
key_sub: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding, alternate interior and alternate exterior angles are equal.
  • Same-side interior angles add to 180°.
  • The angles of a triangle add to 180°. An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
  • Two triangles with two pairs of equal angles are similar (angle-angle).

Examples

Example

∠2 = 65°, ∠2 and ∠6 are corresponding

Corresponding angles are equal

Answer: ∠6 = 65°

Example

Exterior angle with remote angles 40° and 75°

40 + 75

Answer: 115°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking alternate interior angles add to 180°They are equal when the lines are parallel.
Adding the exterior angle to 180°The exterior angle = sum of the two remote interior angles.
Mixing up corresponding and vertical anglesCorresponding angles are in matching corners at each intersection.

A line that crosses two or more other lines.

items.q: ∠1 = 115° and the lines are parallel. Ana says ∠5 = 65°. What did she do wrong?
items.e: Corresponding angles are equal, so ∠5 = 115°. ∠1 and ∠5 are equal, not supplementary.

items.q: A triangle has angles 40° and 60°. Ben says the third angle is 260°. What did he use?
items.e: 360 − 100 = 260. A triangle uses 180°: the third angle is 80°. 360° instead of 180°.

items.q: If same-side interior angles are 75° and 105°, are the lines parallel?
items.e: 75 + 105 = 180, so yes, they add to 180°.
